method: Original connected bilingual manuscript was written first. Sentence-boundary segmentation derives nested counts; all retained late scenes have explicit secondary support, with primary hinges separately identified. No whole-primary-reading certificate.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Стэнли Елнатсу на голову падают кроссовки. Старые, вонючие — как раз то, что нужно отцу, который пытается изобрести способ переработки старой обуви. Стэнли бежит домой с находкой. Полицейскому это кажется подозрительным. Кроссовки принадлежали знаменитому бейсболисту Клайду Ливингстону; их собирались продать на благотворительном аукционе в пользу приюта для бездомных. В историю про подарок с неба никто не верит. Судья предлагает тюрьму или лагерь «Зелёное озеро». Стэнли никогда не бывал в лагере. Может быть, хоть поплавает.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: A pair of sneakers drops onto Stanley Yelnats's head. Old, smelly sneakers: just the thing for his father, who is trying to invent a way to recycle worn-out shoes. Stanley runs home with his find. A police officer thinks this looks suspicious. The sneakers belonged to the famous baseball player Clyde Livingston; a homeless shelter was going to auction them for charity. Nobody believes the story about shoes falling out of the sky. A judge offers Stanley prison or Camp Green Lake. He has never been to camp. Perhaps he will get to swim.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 3 (father’s work), ch. 6; publisher sample pp. 8–10; SparkNotes Summary ch. 6
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Дома у него нет друзей. Над полным, нескладным мальчиком издевается даже Деррик Данн, который гораздо меньше его. В день ареста Деррик бросил его тетрадь в унитаз. Пока Стэнли вытаскивал её, автобус ушёл — поэтому он и оказался под эстакадой.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: He has no friends at home. Even Derrick Dunne, who is much smaller than this heavy, awkward boy, bullies him. On the day of the arrest, Derrick threw his notebook into a toilet. Retrieving it made Stanley miss the bus; that was why he ended up under the overpass.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 3 (bullying), ch. 6 (notebook and missed bus); primary sample pp. 7–8; SparkNotes ch. 6
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: В семье таким несчастьям давно нашли виновника: прапрадеда, якобы укравшего свинью и навлёкшего проклятие. Родители в проклятия не верят, но ругать давно умершего родственника удобно. Зато имя наследуют с удовольствием: в английском Stanley превращается в Yelnats, если читать с конца. Отец — Стэнли Третий, сын — Четвёртый. Их тесная квартира пахнет отцовскими опытами: жжёной резиной и старыми кроссовками.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: His family has a convenient culprit for misfortunes like these: a great-great-grandfather who supposedly stole a pig and brought down a curse. His parents do not believe in curses, but blaming a long-dead relative helps. They are happier to inherit his name: Stanley becomes Yelnats when read backwards. His father is Stanley the Third; he is the Fourth. Their cramped apartment smells of his father's experiments: burning rubber and old sneakers.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 3; publisher sample printed pp. 8–10
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Озера в лагере нет. Вместо него — сухая техасская равнина, изрытая ямами. Стэнли привозят в наручниках. Ему выдают оранжевую одежду, лопату и пустую флягу. Каждый день, без выходных, он должен выкопать яму глубиной и шириной в пять футов — примерно полтора метра. Лопатой проверяют размеры. Якобы так исправляют характер. Начинают до рассвета, пока жара не стала совсем невыносимой. Забора нет: по словам охранника мистера Сэра, единственная вода на сто миль вокруг находится в лагере. Бежать можно. Добежать некуда.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: There is no lake at the camp. There is a dry Texas wasteland pitted with holes. Stanley arrives in handcuffs and receives orange clothes, a shovel and an empty canteen. Every day, including weekends, he must dig a hole five feet deep and five feet across. The shovel measures it. Supposedly this improves his character. Work starts before dawn, before the heat becomes unbearable. There is no fence. According to the guard, Mr. Sir, the camp has the only water for a hundred miles. Stanley can run away. There is nowhere to run to.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 1–4; publisher sample pp. 3–15; Scholastic pp. 26–27
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Единственная приличная тень — под двумя дубами возле домика начальницы. Между дубами висит её гамак. Мальчикам туда нельзя. По высохшему дну ползают скорпионы, змеи и жёлтопятнистые ящерицы, чей укус в этой истории смертелен. Яма может подарить встречу с любой из них.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: The only decent shade is beneath two oaks beside the Warden's cabin. Her hammock hangs between them. The boys are forbidden to use it. Scorpions, snakes and yellow-spotted lizards roam the lakebed; in this story, a lizard's bite is fatal. A hole may hold any of them.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 1; publisher sample pp. 3–4. Death from these fictional lizards is a story-world rule.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Утешений мало: руки быстро покрываются волдырями, а вынутая земля всё время мешает копать дальше. В палатке D тоже приходится разбираться, кто есть кто. Ребята зовут друг друга Подмышкой, Рентгеном, Зигзагом. Воспитателя Пендански прозвали Мамочкой. Стэнли достаётся имя Пещерный человек — куда внушительнее того, как он сам себя чувствует.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: There is little comfort in digging: blisters rise on Stanley's hands, and the dirt he has dug out keeps getting in his way. In Tent D he must also learn who is who. The boys call one another Armpit, X-Ray and Zigzag. Their counselor, Mr. Pendanski, is Mom. Stanley becomes Caveman, a name considerably more impressive than he feels.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 5–7, 9; Scholastic pp. 27, 41–45; SparkNotes ch. 7
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: А задолго до этого, в Латвии, его прапрадед Эля Елнатс хотел жениться на Майре Менке. Другой жених мог предложить её отцу большую свинью; у Эли такой не было. Старая мадам Зерони считала затею глупой, но всё-таки дала ему поросёнка. Каждый день Эля должен был нести его на гору, поить из ручья и петь особую песню. Поросёнок рос; Эля постепенно становился достаточно сильным, чтобы носить его. Взамен он обещал однажды поднять туда саму мадам Зерони, дать ей напиться и спеть. За невыполненное обещание она пригрозила проклятием его потомкам.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Long before this, in Latvia, his great-great-grandfather Elya Yelnats wanted to marry Myra Menke. Another suitor could offer her father a large pig; Elya could not. Old Madame Zeroni thought the whole scheme foolish, but she gave him a piglet anyway. Each day he was to carry it up a mountain, let it drink from a stream and sing a particular song. The pig grew; Elya gradually became strong enough to carry it. In return, he promised to carry Madame Zeroni up there herself, give her water and sing. She threatened a curse on his descendants if he broke his promise.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 7; Scholastic pp. 28, 36, 42; Sachar Q&A on Elya and broken promise; SparkNotes ch. 7
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Когда пришло время свататься, оказалось, что Майре почти всё равно, за кого выходить. Разочарованный Эля уехал в Америку и забыл о старухе. Потом он жалел, что так и не отнёс её к ручью. В Америке у него появилась семья; песню он передал жене, а дальше её пели детям. Неудачи тоже продолжались.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: When the time came to claim Myra, it turned out that she hardly cared whom she married. Disappointed, Elya sailed for America and forgot the old woman. Afterwards he regretted never carrying her to the stream. He made a family in America and taught his wife the song; it passed down to their children. Misfortunes continued too.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 7; Scholastic pp. 28, 36; primary Elya-remorse quotation embedded on p. 36; SparkNotes ch. 7
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Сын Эли, первый Стэнли Елнатс, сумел разбогатеть — но разбойница Поцелуйная Кейт Барлоу ограбила его и оставила в пустыне. Он выжил. Для нынешнего Стэнли иметь в семье человека, ограбленного знаменитой преступницей, даже немного почётно, хотя дом на берегу океана ему понравился бы больше.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Elya's son, the first Stanley Yelnats, managed to make a fortune, but the outlaw Kissin' Kate Barlow robbed him and abandoned him in the desert. He survived. To the present Stanley, having someone in the family robbed by a famous outlaw is even a little impressive, though he would have preferred a house beside the ocean.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 3; publisher sample pp. 9–10; Scholastic pp. 26–27. Elya is great-great-grandfather, robbed Stanley I is great-grandfather.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: На высохшем озере день за днём Стэнли становится крепче. Он уже не совсем чужой среди мальчиков и пишет матери о лагере так, будто всё идёт неплохо: появились друзья, целый день провели на озере. Мать не должна волноваться.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: On the dry lake, Stanley grows stronger day by day. He is no longer quite an outsider among the boys. He writes to his mother as though camp is going well: he has made friends; they have spent the day out on the lake. She must not worry.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 9; Scholastic pp. 27, 43–44, including short primary letter excerpt
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Рентген, неофициальный главарь группы, просит отдавать ему интересные находки: за них можно получить выходной. Когда Стэнли выкапывает золотистый футляр с буквами KB, он выполняет уговор. Рентген выдаёт вещицу за собственную находку. Начальница немедленно оживляется и велит усиленно рыть рядом. Стэнли понимает: ищут что-то определённое. Только ищут не там, где он нашёл футляр.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: X-Ray, the group's unofficial leader, asks Stanley to hand over anything interesting he finds: a discovery might earn a day off. When Stanley digs up a gold-colored tube marked KB, he keeps the agreement. X-Ray presents it as his own find. The Warden immediately takes an interest and orders concentrated digging nearby. Stanley realizes they are looking for something specific. But they are looking somewhere other than where he found the tube.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 11–15; Scholastic p. 27, including primary wrong-place quotation
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Самого молчаливого мальчика зовут Зеро — Ноль. Пендански любит объяснять прозвище отсутствием мыслей в его голове. Зеро не умеет читать, но умеет считать в уме; он гораздо внимательнее, чем окружающим удобно замечать. Он просит Стэнли научить его буквам. Тот сначала отказывается.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: The quietest boy is called Zero. Pendanski enjoys explaining the nickname by saying there is nothing inside his head. Zero cannot read, but he can do arithmetic in his head. He notices much more than other people find convenient. He asks Stanley to teach him his letters. Stanley refuses at first.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 18, 22; SparkNotes Summary ch. 18 confirms the initial request/refusal; Scholastic pp. 39, 45–46; Bloomsbury Q10 primary fragment; SparkNotes ch. 22
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Потом Стэнли берёт на себя вину за украденные у мистера Сэра семечки и попадает к начальнице. Она царапает охраннику лицо ногтями, покрытыми лаком с ядом гремучей змеи. Боль достаётся охраннику, а за водой после этого особенно трудно становится Стэнли. Вернувшись к своей яме, мальчик видит, что Зеро уже поработал за него.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Then Stanley takes the blame for some sunflower seeds stolen from Mr. Sir and is brought before the Warden. She scratches the guard's face with nails coated in rattlesnake-venom polish. The guard gets the pain, and Stanley subsequently has particular trouble getting water. When Stanley returns to his hole, he finds that Zero has done some digging for him.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 19–22, 24; SparkNotes Summary ch. 19 confirms the seed incident; Scholastic p. 43; Sachar Q&A on venom polish; Bloomsbury Q11–12; SparkNotes chs. 20–24
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Позже Стэнли соглашается учить его читать. Они договариваются: Зеро час копает за Стэнли, чтобы у того хватало сил на урок. За молчанием обнаруживается быстрый ум. Постепенно Зеро учится писать собственное имя: Гектор Зерони. У Стэнли появляется друг, но остальные недовольны тем, что часть его работы делает другой.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Later Stanley agrees to teach him to read. They make a deal: Zero will dig for Stanley for an hour, leaving him enough energy for the lesson. Behind the silence Stanley discovers a quick mind. Zero gradually learns to write his own name: Hector Zeroni. Stanley has a friend, but the other boys resent someone doing part of his work.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 22, 27; Scholastic pp. 28, 45–46; SparkNotes chs. 22, 27
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: А золотой футляр получает возможное объяснение: у начальницы Стэнли видел похожую вещь для губной помады. Неужели KB — Кейт Барлоу, та самая разбойница из семейной истории?
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Meanwhile, the gold tube has a possible explanation. At the Warden's cabin Stanley saw a similar container for lipstick. Could KB stand for Kate Barlow, the outlaw from his family history?
screens.locations: Novel ch. 22; Scholastic p. 27; SparkNotes ch. 22. Stanley’s identification is still a question here.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Сто с лишним лет назад Кэтрин Барлоу была учительницей в городке у настоящего Зелёного озера. На берегу росли персиковые деревья; она готовила знаменитые пряные персики. Сэм продавал лук и чинил ей школу в обмен на угощение. Они разговаривали, и Кэтрин всё находила, что ещё нужно починить. Сэм был чернокожим: работать в школе ему позволяли, учиться в ней — нет.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: More than a century earlier, Katherine Barlow taught school beside a real Green Lake. Peach trees grew along its shore, and she made famous spiced peaches. Sam sold onions and repaired her schoolhouse in exchange for treats. They talked, and Katherine kept finding things for him to fix. Sam was Black: he could work in the school but was not allowed to attend it.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 23, 25; Scholastic pp. 28, 33; SparkNotes chs. 23, 25
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Богатый Чарльз Уокер, прозванный Форелью за неприятный запах ног, хотел жениться на Кэтрин. Она отказалась даже прокатиться с ним на его новой моторной лодке. С Сэмом ей было хорошо. Их поцелуй увидели в городе.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Wealthy Charles Walker, nicknamed Trout because of his terrible foot odor, wanted to marry Katherine. She refused even a ride in his new motorboat. With Sam she was happy. Someone in town saw them kiss.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 23, 25; Scholastic pp. 28, 42; SparkNotes chs. 23, 25
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Белая учительница поцеловалась с чернокожим мужчиной — и город поднялся против них. Толпа разгромила школу. Кэтрин побежала к шерифу, но тот не собирался защищать Сэма: сам заговорил о виселице и потребовал поцелуй. Кэтрин и Сэм попытались уйти по озеру. Лодка Уокера была быстрее. Сэма убили. После этого, рассказывает роман, дождь над Зелёным озером перестал идти.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: A white teacher has kissed a Black man, and the town turns against them. A mob wrecked the schoolhouse. Katherine ran to the sheriff, but he had no intention of protecting Sam: he spoke of hanging him and demanded a kiss himself. Katherine and Sam tried to escape across the lake. Walker's boat was faster. Sam was killed. After that, the novel relates, rain stopped falling on Green Lake.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 26; Scholastic pp. 28, 36; author Q&A about Kate/Sam; SparkNotes ch. 26
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Через три дня Кэтрин застрелила шерифа и оставила поцелуй на его мёртвом лице. Так появилась Поцелуйная Кейт, двадцать лет грабившая на Западе. Когда она вернулась к высыхающему озеру, Уокер с женой Линдой стали пытать её, добиваясь места, где спрятана добыча. Укус жёлтопятнистой ящерицы оборвал её жизнь. Тайну она им не выдала.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Three days later Katherine shot the sheriff and kissed his dead face. She became Kissin' Kate, an outlaw who robbed people across the West for twenty years. When she returned to the dwindling lake, Walker and his wife Linda tortured her to learn where she had buried her loot. A yellow-spotted lizard bit her, ending her life. She never gave them the hiding place.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 26, 28; Scholastic p. 28 with primary sheriff/outlaw quotation; author Q&A on torture; SparkNotes chs. 26, 28
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: В лагере гроза вспыхивает над далёкими горами, но дождя нет. В свете молнии Стэнли различает скалу, похожую на поднятый большой палец. Его прадед после спасения из пустыни говорил, что укрылся на Божьем пальце.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: At camp a storm flashes over distant mountains, bringing no rain. In the lightning Stanley glimpses a rock shaped like a raised thumb. After being rescued from the desert, his great-grandfather had said he found refuge on God's thumb.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 21, 29; Scholastic p. 29 primary refuge fragment; SparkNotes chs. 21, 29
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Тем временем ссора вокруг уроков перерастает в драку: Зигзаг нападает на Стэнли, Зеро вступается. Начальница запрещает уроки. Пендански снова издевается над Зеро, уверяя, что тот годится только копать. Зеро бьёт его лопатой по лицу и уходит в пустыню. Взрослые рассчитывают, что жажда вернёт беглеца. Остальным велят выкопать и его яму.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Meanwhile, the quarrel over the lessons becomes a fight. Zigzag attacks Stanley; Zero intervenes. The Warden forbids the lessons. Pendanski mocks Zero again, saying digging is all he is good for. Zero hits him in the face with his shovel and walks into the desert. The adults expect thirst to bring the runaway back. The others are ordered to dig his hole as well.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 30; Scholastic pp. 28–29, 46; Bloomsbury Q3/Q15 do not supply unquoted motives; SparkNotes ch. 30
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Дни проходят, Зеро не возвращается. Стэнли слышит, как взрослые собираются уничтожить его записи: мальчика всё равно никто не станет искать. Его мучает мысль, что помогать уже поздно. Ещё хуже другая: вдруг пока не поздно, а он ничего не делает?
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Days pass without Zero returning. Stanley hears the adults planning to erase his records: nobody will look for him anyway. He is tormented by the thought that it is too late to help. Worse is the possibility that it is not too late and he is doing nothing.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 31; Scholastic pp. 29–30, 44 includes primary not-too-late quotation; SparkNotes ch. 31
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Когда к ним подъезжает машина с водой, Стэнли пытается угнать её. Водить он не умеет и почти сразу загоняет грузовик в яму. Тогда бежит пешком. Впереди — сухое дно, жара и далёкая гора. Долгое время он не находит ничего, кроме новых ям.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: When the water truck arrives, he tries to steal it. He cannot drive and almost immediately runs it into a hole. Then he runs on foot. Ahead lie the dry lakebed, the heat and a distant mountain. For a long time he finds nothing but more holes.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 32–34; Scholastic pp. 36–37; SparkNotes chs. 32–34. Last narrative scene in Essential/Core.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Потом в пыли появляется перевёрнутая лодка с именем «Мэри Лу». Под ней прячется Зеро. Он выжил на старых банках с персиковой массой, которую назвал «сплуш». Живот у него сильно болит, но возвращаться он отказывается. Последнюю банку он делит со Стэнли. Лодка Сэма и персики Кэтрин пережили свой город; теперь возле них встретились два беглеца.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Then an overturned boat appears in the dust, with the name Mary Lou on it. Zero is hiding beneath it. He has survived on old jars of peach mush, which he calls sploosh. His stomach hurts badly, but he refuses to go back. He shares the last jar with Stanley. Sam's boat and Katherine's peaches have outlasted their town; now the two runaways have met beside them.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 34–35; Scholastic pp. 35, 46; SparkNotes chs. 34–35. Primary continuous chapters not read.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Они выбираются к горе. Даже больной Зеро помогает Стэнли подняться на уступ, удерживая лопату и раня себе руки. Потом он теряет силы. Дальше Стэнли несёт друга сам.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: They head for the mountain. Even sick, Zero helps Stanley up a ledge, gripping the shovel and cutting his own hands. Then his strength gives out. Stanley carries him the rest of the way.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 36–38; Scholastic pp. 29, 46; SparkNotes chs. 36–38
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Наверху есть влажная земля, вода и дикий лук. Мальчики едят, пьют и остаются жить на склоне. Всё ещё больной Зеро признаётся: кроссовки Ливингстона украл он. Стэнли поёт больному Зеро старую семейную песню.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: At the top there are damp earth, water and wild onions. The boys eat, drink and stay on the mountainside. Still sick, Zero confesses: he stole Livingston's sneakers. Stanley sings the sick Zero an old family song.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 38–40; Scholastic p. 29; SparkNotes chs. 38–40 explicitly orders confession before singing
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Это та песня, которую мадам Зерони когда-то научила петь Элю. Праправнук Эли принёс к воде прапраправнука мадам Зерони: старый уговор исполнился через поколения, хотя мальчики своей родословной не знают. Мать Стэнли, впрочем, так и не поверит, что проклятие существовало.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: It is the song Madame Zeroni taught Elya. Elya's great-great-grandson has carried Madame Zeroni's great-great-great-grandson up to water: the old promise has been fulfilled across generations, although the boys do not know their ancestry. Stanley's mother, however, will still insist there never was a curse.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 39, 43, 50; Scholastic pp. 29, 35–38 (primary narrator lineage quotation p. 35); Bloomsbury Q23 primary mother quotation; SparkNotes chs. 39, 43, 50
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Позже Зеро объясняет, как всё случилось. Не прочитав табличку в приюте, он взял старую пару, полагая, что это лучше, чем красть новую. Когда поднялся шум, оставил обувь на припаркованной машине. Так начался путь кроссовок, которые потом свалились на Стэнли. Самого Зеро арестовали за другую пару.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Later Zero explains how it happened. Unable to read the notice at the shelter, he took an old pair, thinking that better than stealing new ones. When the alarm went up, he left them on a parked car. That began the journey of the shoes that later dropped onto Stanley. Zero himself was arrested for another pair.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 39, 41; Scholastic pp. 44–45; Bloomsbury Q17 distinguishes the later shoe theft; SparkNotes chs. 39, 41. Parked car, not film’s thrown shoes.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Он рассказывает и о матери: однажды она велела ждать её в парке и не вернулась. Он ждал больше месяца и ночевал внутри трубы на детской площадке. Стэнли знает этот парк — сам там играл. Зеро тоже знает эту песню с детства: мать пела ему похожую, с другими словами.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: He also tells Stanley about his mother: one day she told him to wait in a park and did not return. He waited for more than a month, sleeping inside a tunnel on the playground. Stanley knows the park; he played there himself. Zero knows the song from childhood too: his mother sang a version with different words.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 43; Scholastic p. 46 primary park/month/tunnel conversation; SparkNotes ch. 43. Mother’s private reasons not invented.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Зеро поправляется. Стэнли помнит место, где на самом деле лежал золотой футляр; начальница копала совсем в другом месте. Они решают вернуться к лагерю, а ночью поискать клад и уйти. Набирают воду в банки, берут лук.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Zero recovers. Stanley remembers where the gold tube really lay; the Warden was digging in quite the wrong place. They decide to return to camp, look for the treasure after dark and leave. They fill jars with water and take onions.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 42–44; Scholastic p. 29; SparkNotes chs. 42–44
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: В яме удаётся откопать металлический чемодан. И тут их освещает фонарь: над ними стоит начальница. Но взять добычу она не может. По чемодану и мальчикам ползают жёлтопятнистые ящерицы. Стэнли попал прямо в гнездо. Мальчики не двигаются, взрослые ждут их смерти и обсуждают, как объяснить случившееся. Ночь тянется. Выясняется, что начальница — внучка Форели Уокера и с детства искала здесь клад вместе с родителями.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: In the hole they manage to uncover a metal suitcase. Then a flashlight shines on them: the Warden is standing above. But she cannot take the prize. Yellow-spotted lizards are crawling over the suitcase and the boys. Stanley has dug straight into a nest. The boys keep still while the adults wait for them to die and discuss how to explain what happened. The night drags on. The Warden turns out to be Trout Walker's granddaughter; she grew up searching here with her parents.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 44–46; Scholastic pp. 29, 38–39 (primary childhood-digging quotation p. 39); Sachar Q&A confirms Warden/Trout ancestry; SparkNotes chs. 44–46
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: К утру приезжает адвокат Стэнли, госпожа Моренго, с генеральным прокурором штата. Стэнли признали невиновным; его должны отпустить. Начальница пытается объявить чемодан своей собственностью. Но Зеро уже умеет читать. На другой стороне он разобрал имя: Stanley Yelnats. Чемодан принадлежал тому самому прадеду, которого когда-то ограбила Кейт. Одинаковые имена в семье вдруг оказываются очень кстати.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: By morning Stanley's lawyer, Ms. Morengo, arrives with the state Attorney General. Stanley has been cleared and must be released. The Warden tries to claim the suitcase as her property. But Zero can read now. On the other side he has deciphered a name: Stanley Yelnats. It belonged to the very great-grandfather Kate robbed. The family's habit of repeating names has suddenly become extremely useful.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 47–48; Scholastic p. 30; SparkNotes chs. 47–48; primary name lineage ch. 3 and author interview in Scholastic p. 17 support ancestor identity
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Стэнли отказывается уходить без Гектора. Моренго требует его документы; записи уничтожены, и лагерь даже не может объяснить, почему держит мальчика. Она увозит обоих. Позже Моренго объясняет, почему Стэнли оправдали: именно Деррик подтвердил, что в момент кражи тот ещё вытаскивал из унитаза тетрадь. Мальчик, из-за которого Стэнли оказался под эстакадой, невольно обеспечил ему алиби.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Stanley refuses to leave without Hector. Morengo demands his records; they have been destroyed, and the camp cannot even explain why it is holding him. She takes both boys away. Later Morengo explains why Stanley was cleared: Derrick confirmed that at the time of the theft he was still fishing his notebook out of the toilet. The boy who made Stanley end up under the overpass has unwittingly given him an alibi.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 48–49; Scholastic pp. 30, 40 (primary notebook/alibi quotation on p. 40); SparkNotes chs. 48–49
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: В машине из-за их лукового запаха приходится открывать окна. Ящерицы не кусали их по той же причине: Сэм когда-то продавал охотникам луковый сок для защиты от них. Дни на луковом поле, едва позволившие мальчикам выжить, потом спасли их в гнезде.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: In the car their onion smell means the windows have to stay open. The lizards did not bite for the same reason: Sam used to sell hunters onion juice to protect them from the creatures. The days in the onion field, which barely enabled the boys to survive, later saved them in the nest.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 49; Scholastic pp. 29, 33 establish onions; SparkNotes Summary ch. 49 explicitly explains the fictional lizard protection. Not zoological evidence.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Впервые за сто с лишним лет над озером идёт дождь. Лагерь закрывают, начальница продаёт землю; на этом месте собираются открыть лагерь для девочек-скаутов — мистер Сэр столько раз напоминал, что здесь не скауты.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: For the first time in more than a century, rain falls on the lake. The camp closes and the Warden sells the land; a Girl Scout camp is planned for the site, after Mr. Sir's repeated reminders that this was no Girl Scout camp.
screens.locations: Novel chs. 49–50; Scholastic pp. 30, 39; SparkNotes chs. 49–50. Scout irony recalls direct primary ch. 4.
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: В чемодане оказываются драгоценности и ценные бумаги. Стэнли делится находкой с Гектором. Семья Елнатсов покупает дом, Гектор нанимает сыщика, чтобы найти мать. Отец Стэнли тем временем изобретает средство от запаха ног, пахнущее персиками. Рассказчик отмечает: удача пришла на следующий день после того, как Стэнли поднял Зеро на гору.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: The suitcase holds jewels and valuable financial papers. Stanley shares the find with Hector. The Yelnats family buys a house; Hector hires an investigator to find his mother. Meanwhile, Stanley's father invents a cure for foot odor that smells of peaches. The narrator notes that his luck changed the day after Stanley carried Zero up the mountain.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 50; Scholastic pp. 30, 35 (primary invention timing quotation); SparkNotes ch. 50
screens.primaryScopeLimit: Only the stated sample and embedded short primary quotations were read; guide chapter coverage is not continuous reading of those novel chapters.

screens.retainedClaimsRU: Позже все смотрят рекламу отцовского средства: в ней снялся Клайд Ливингстон. Сам бейсболист тоже сидит у Елнатсов перед телевизором. У Гектора рядом женщина с такими же глазами и знакомой улыбкой — мать, которую он нашёл. Она поёт ему старую песню. Рядом с ним наконец тот человек, которого он так долго ждал.
screens.retainedClaimsEN: Later, everyone watches an advertisement for the invention, starring Clyde Livingston. The baseball player himself is sitting with the Yelnatses in front of the television. Beside Hector is a woman with eyes like his and a familiar smile: the mother he has found. She sings him the old song. Beside him at last is the person he waited for so long.
screens.locations: Novel ch. 50; Scholastic pp. 38, 45–46 for relationship and family descriptions; SparkNotes Summary ch. 50 for final gathering. No film arrests or grandfather scene imported.
